h1: The 6 Best Compact Wet-Dry Vacuums for Garages and Small Spaces, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Compact Wet-Dry Vacuums: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 compact wet-dry vacuums compared on tank size, filtration, hose reach and storage footprint, from under $50 to $100.
summary: The CRAFTSMAN 2.5 gallon model is the compact wet-dry vac to buy for most garages and workshops, because it balances tank size, suction and storage footprint at a budget price. The WEN 5 gallon is the pick when fine drywall or sanding dust is the real problem, the Vacmaster 3.2 gallon is the best mid-size step up, and the Armor All 1.5 gallon is the cheapest way to get a small bucket vac into a car trunk or closet.
intro: Most people shop for a compact shop vac by looking at one number, peak horsepower, and that is where the trouble starts. Peak horsepower is measured in a way no household circuit can sustain, so a 2 peak HP unit and a 2.5 peak HP unit may sound a lot alike once they are running. The things that actually change your experience are tank size, hose diameter, filter type and how much floor space the machine eats when you put it away.

This ranking sorts six small wet-dry vacuums with that in mind. We reviewed the listings and spec sheets, kept the tank sizes and motor ratings as the manufacturers publish them, and judged each machine on how well it fits the job of a small garage, a car, a basement corner or a workshop bench. Where a listing does not state something, we say so rather than guess.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN CMXEVBE17250 2.5 Gallon 2.5 Peak HP Wet Dry Shop Vacuum
products.verdict: The right-sized shop vac for a one-car garage: small enough to hang on a wall, strong enough to matter.
products.description:
The CRAFTSMAN is a 2.5 gallon unit with a 2.5 peak HP motor, and it sits in the sweet spot between a toy-sized bucket vac and a full 5 gallon machine. That tank holds enough to clear a spilled bag of potting soil or a flooded utility sink corner without stopping every few minutes to empty it.

It takes first place because it is the most balanced machine here. It has more capacity than the 1.5 gallon Armor All, it costs noticeably less than the Vacmaster below it, and the brand name brings accessory availability that off-brand models sometimes lack. Compared with the WEN it gives up the HEPA-style filter and blower function, so it is a general-purpose cleaner rather than a fine-dust specialist.

Buy it for garage cleanups, car interiors, basement drips and light workshop debris. The caveat is the usual one for any small wet-dry vac: the stock filter is not meant for drywall dust, and the cord and hose are short enough that a large room means an extension cord.
pros: Tank size suits garages and car interiors
Strong brand means easy accessory finding
Budget price for a 2.5 peak HP motor
Small enough to hang on a shelf
cons: Stock filter struggles with fine dust
Short cord needs an extension often
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants one small vac for the garage, car and basement.
products.skipIf: You sand drywall or clean fine ash and need real filtration.

products.name: WEN VC4710 10-Amp 5-Gallon Portable HEPA Wet/Dry Shop Vacuum and Blower with 0.3-Micron Filter, Hose, and Accessories,Orange
products.verdict: A 5 gallon vac with a 0.3-micron filter and a blower port, aimed at dust rather than puddles.
products.description:
The VC4710 is a 5 gallon portable vacuum drawing 10 amps, and its headline feature is a filter rated down to 0.3 microns. It also doubles as a blower and ships with a hose and an accessory set, so the box covers most small jobs without extra purchases.

It ranks second because it is the biggest and most capable machine here, but also the least compact. The filter is the real reason to choose it: ordinary paper cartridges clog and leak fine particles back into the room, while a finer filter keeps sanding residue and workshop dust out of the air you breathe. The tradeoff against the CRAFTSMAN is footprint and weight, since a 5 gallon tank takes noticeably more wall or floor space.

Choose it for a workshop, a woodworking corner or a renovation job where dust control matters. Skip it if your closet is tight or you only need to grab spills, because the extra capacity will just be in the way.
pros: Fine 0.3-micron filter traps workshop dust
Blower port adds a second use
Hose and accessories come in the box
Largest tank means fewer emptying trips
products.idealFor: Woodworkers and renovators who care about the dust they breathe.
products.skipIf: Storage space is tight or you only clean up liquid spills.

products.name: Vacmaster VHB305M 1101 3.2-Gal 2.5 Peak HP Compact Wet/Dry Vacuum Red
products.verdict: A 3.2 gallon compact build that stores in tight spots yet holds more than the 2.5 gallon models.
products.description:
The VHB305M pairs a 3.2 gallon tank with a 2.5 peak HP motor, which puts its motor rating level with the CRAFTSMAN while giving about a quarter more room in the canister. Vacmaster describes it as a compact model, and the listing positions it as a pick for the tightest storage spaces.

It lands third because it costs more than the two cheapest machines without adding a headline feature the others lack. What it does give you is a small body with a bit more capacity, which matters when you vacuum a whole car or a small shop in one go. Vacmaster's pro-tool heritage also suggests sturdier parts, though the listing gives no warranty detail we can quote.

It suits apartment dwellers, van owners and anyone with a utility closet shelf rather than a garage wall. If you have the room for a 5 gallon machine, the WEN does more for similar money.
pros: Compact body stores on a small shelf
Tank holds more than 2.5 gallon rivals
Motor rating matches the top pick
Suits apartments and vans well
cons: Costs more than similar small models
No special filter listed for dust
products.idealFor: Apartment and van owners who need maximum tank per square foot.
products.skipIf: You have garage space and want the larger 5 gallon option.

products.name: Armor All AA255W 2.5 Gal 2 Peak HP Wet/Dry Utility Vac Orange/Black
products.verdict: A simple 2.5 gallon utility vac that asks nothing of a first-time buyer.
products.description:
The AA255W is a 2.5 gallon wet/dry utility vac with a 2 peak HP motor, sold under the Armor All car-care name. The listing frames it as a first-time purchase, and the layout reflects that: a small tank, a standard hose and no complicated settings.

It ranks fourth because it matches the CRAFTSMAN on tank size but sits in the higher price bucket and carries the lower 2 peak HP rating. Peak horsepower is a marketing figure, so the gap may feel small in use, yet the price comparison is hard to ignore. The Armor All name does suggest cleaning accessories aimed at cars, which is the strongest use for it.

Buy it as a car-and-garage starter or as a gift for someone who has never owned a shop vac. If you can stretch to the CRAFTSMAN for less money, that is the better value.
pros: Simple controls suit first-time owners
Tank size covers car interior cleanups
Recognizable car-care brand name
Light enough to carry one-handed
products.idealFor: First-time buyers who mainly want to clean a car.
products.skipIf: Value matters and you can choose the CRAFTSMAN instead.

products.name: Armor All® AA155 1.5-Gallon 2 Peak HP Portable Wet/Dry Vacuum, Orange
products.verdict: The smallest tank in the group, priced for people who want a vac that disappears into a closet.
products.description:
The AA155 is a 1.5 gallon portable wet/dry vacuum with a 2 peak HP motor, the smallest tank in this ranking. The listing sells it on compact performance for less, and the budget price bucket backs that up.

It ranks fifth because the small tank forces frequent stops. A 1.5 gallon bucket fills quickly with wet debris, and liquid is heavy, so you will empty it more often than any other model here. In exchange you get a light machine that fits behind a seat or on a closet shelf and makes light spills trivial.

It is the right choice for a dorm, a small rental or a car trunk where space is the limiting factor. Skip it for flooded basements or any job that produces more than a bucket of mess.
pros: Smallest and lightest body in the group
Budget price for wet and dry duty
Easy to stash in a car trunk
Light spills clean up in seconds
cons: Not suited for large liquid spills
products.idealFor: Dorms, small rentals and car trunks with almost no storage.
products.skipIf: You expect to vacuum water or debris by the bucket.

products.name: Amazon Basics Wet Dry Shop Vacuum Cleaner, 4 Gallon, 3 HP Stainless Steel, Grey/Black
products.verdict: A 4 gallon stainless-steel tank with a 3 HP rating, the biggest motor claim on this list.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics vacuum pairs a 4 gallon stainless-steel tank with a 3 HP rating, the highest motor figure among the six. Stainless steel is a sensible choice for the canister because it resists dents and rust better than thin plastic.

It ranks last here because its size pushes it out of the true compact class, and the listing gives few details about filtration or accessories. A 3 HP rating sounds powerful but follows the same peak-style marketing as the rest, so it does not guarantee stronger suction than the 2.5 peak HP models. Against the Vacmaster it offers more tank capacity, but it is bulkier to store.

It works for a garage owner who wants a bigger bin without paying for the WEN's filter. If the vacuum will live in a closet or trunk, choose a smaller model.
pros: Stainless-steel tank resists dents and rust
Holds more debris than 2.5 gallon rivals
Highest motor rating on the list
Plain design with few parts to break
cons: Bulkier than a true compact vac
Few filtration details on the listing
products.idealFor: Garage owners who want a larger metal tank on a budget.
products.skipIf: Your storage is a closet shelf or a car trunk.

methodology.title: Tank size versus footprint
methodology.description: We compared each gallon rating to the space the machine plausibly takes, because a vac that is too big to store ends up unused.

methodology.title: Motor and airflow claims
methodology.description: Peak horsepower and amp ratings were read as manufacturer marketing figures, so we leaned on tank size, filter type and accessories to separate similar machines.

methodology.title: Filtration
methodology.description: Models with a documented fine filter scored higher for dust jobs, while basic cartridges were judged as fine for spills and general debris.

methodology.title: Build and materials
methodology.description: Stainless tanks, brand heritage and accessory availability counted toward durability, since the listings rarely publish warranty detail.

methodology.title: Value for the price bucket
methodology.description: Each pick was judged against the others in its price bracket, rewarding machines that give more capacity or features for the same spend.

whatMatters.detail: The gallon figure decides how often you stop to empty the canister, and wet debris fills it faster than dry because liquid is heavy. For car interiors and small spills, 1.5 to 2.5 gallons is workable; for a garage or workshop floor, 3 to 5 gallons saves real time. Check the number in the title of the listing and compare it with the space you can spare for storage.

Peak horsepower is the highest output a motor reaches in a lab spin-up, not what it sustains while pulling air through a hose. Two vacuums rated 2 and 2.5 peak HP can feel nearly identical in use. Look instead for amp draw, tank size and hose diameter, and treat the horsepower figure as a rough tier rather than a promise.

A standard paper or foam filter handles water and household debris, but fine dust such as drywall, sanding residue or cold ash passes through or clogs it quickly. A 0.3-micron rated filter, like the WEN lists, keeps those particles out of the exhaust air. If you only vacuum spills and leaves, do not pay extra for it.

A short or narrow hose limits reach and clogs on larger debris such as wood chips or wet leaves. Check the listing for hose length and diameter, and expect to use an extension cord with small units, since cords are usually short. A longer hose often matters more than extra tank size for car and stair work.

Compact is the whole point, so measure the shelf, closet or trunk space first. Round canisters stack and tuck into corners, while the small ones with a top handle hang on a wall hook. The accessories matter too, since a tool-storage clip or a wrapped cord can keep the machine tidy instead of sprawling.

howToChoose.intro: Choose the smallest tank that handles your biggest regular mess, because every extra gallon costs storage space.

cards.label: Standard filter
cards.text: A basic cartridge is fine for spills, leaves, pet hair and general garage debris. The CRAFTSMAN, Vacmaster and both Armor All models fall into this group.

cards.label: Fine-dust filter
cards.text: A 0.3-micron filter captures sanding dust and drywall residue instead of blowing it back out. The WEN VC4710 is the pick in this ranking.

howToChoose.note: Default to the CRAFTSMAN unless you regularly make fine dust.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A light body, a hose long enough to reach the back seat and a tank you can empty without fuss. Crevice and brush tools matter more than raw horsepower.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Armor All AA255W and AA155 are built around car-care use, while the CRAFTSMAN gives more capacity if you also clean the garage.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You make fine dust, run the vac for long jobs or want accessories in the box. The WEN VC4710 and the Vacmaster VHB305M reward that spend.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You vacuum light spills and leaves a few times a year. The CRAFTSMAN or the Armor All AA155 covers that comfortably.

faq.q: Can a compact wet-dry vac pick up water?
faq.a: Yes, that is what the wet/dry label means, and all six machines here are designed for it. Remove any paper filter and use the foam sleeve or wet-rated filter the manual specifies, then empty the tank promptly so the motor stays dry.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with small shop vacs?
faq.a: Using the standard filter for drywall or sanding dust. Fine particles clog the cartridge within minutes and pass into the room air. If you create that kind of dust, pick a model with a fine filter such as the WEN, or add a separation bag.

faq.q: Is a 5 gallon vac worth it over a 2.5 gallon one?
faq.a: Only if you vacuum large volumes or want better filtration. The 5 gallon WEN holds twice the debris and has a finer filter, but it is bulkier to store and heavier to carry. For car and light garage work, the smaller CRAFTSMAN is easier to live with.

faq.q: Do I need an extension cord?
faq.a: Usually yes. Compact vacs ship with short cords to keep cost and weight down, so cleaning a full garage or driveway often needs a heavy-duty extension. Check the cord length in the listing and use a gauge that suits the motor's amp draw.

faq.q: How should I clean the filter and tank?
faq.a: Empty the tank after every wet job, rinse it, and let it air dry before storing so mold does not build up. Tap dry filters out over a bin and replace them when the airflow drops, because a clogged filter is the main reason suction fades.

faq.q: Can I use these as blowers?
faq.a: Only if the listing says so. The WEN VC4710 lists a blower function, which is handy for clearing leaves or drying a workbench. The others are suction-only unless the manual describes a blower port, so check before relying on it.

finalTake: For most buyers the CRAFTSMAN CMXEVBE17250 is the one to get, because it combines a 2.5 gallon tank, a decent motor and a small footprint at a low price. Step up to the WEN VC4710 if fine dust is part of your work, or to the Vacmaster if you need the tightest storage with a bit more capacity. Pick the Armor All AA155 only when trunk space is your limit.
